note: Verification re-run of the two layers that runtime device PM touches, after two changes on top of the earlier run of the same day: the NULL guard in pd_pm_action() (drivers/power_domain/power_domain_soc_state_change.c, not yet committed) and the corrected boot-state expectation in both samples, which now accept OFF as well as SUSPENDED for a device that names a power domain. The vref case is recorded in the companion file with the same run id.

frdm_mcxn947/mcxn947/cpu0.note: Both layers now boot and both pass. Every pin-mux reports OFF at init with its clock gate open, runtime_get takes it to ACTIVE, runtime_put back to SUSPENDED, and the gate never closes -- which is the claim the case exists to make. The constraint checks in the system layer pass unchanged.

findings.detail: Returning 0 from pd_pm_action() when pm_state_next_get() reports NULL. Before the guard both layers captured zero bytes on this board; after it they run to a verdict. See results/20260916-port-dapeng.json for the analysis.
